## Natural history notes

A rough-bodied hide beetle characterized by its dark, oval body, bumpy sculptured wing covers, and dusty or soil-covered appearance that helps it blend into dry organic material. In Florida, the Hide Beetle is found in sandy open areas, dry fields, scrub, pine flatwoods, roadsides, coastal habitats, and around animal remains or dry carrion. Adults and larvae feed on dried carrion, hides, feathers, bones, and other tough animal material, helping break down remains during later stages of decomposition while also serving as prey for birds, reptiles, spiders, and predatory insects.
